---

> This document defines comprehensive accessibility standards for enterprise applications, providing guidance on WCAG 2.2 AA compliance requirements, technical implementation patterns, semantic HTML, ARIA implementation, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast, testing strategies, and development tools to ensure applications are usable by people with a wide range of abilities and meet regulatory compliance requirements.

## 1.0 Overview

This document establishes comprehensive accessibility standards for all enterprise applications, ensuring they are usable by people with a wide range of abilities and meet compliance requirements. These standards align with WCAG 2.2 AA guidelines and legal requirements while providing practical implementation guidance for development teams.
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/accessibility/STD-APP-ACC-001-accessibility.md#21-wcag-22-aa-compliance]

### 2.1 WCAG 2.2 AA Compliance

All user interfaces must comply with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at the AA level:

1. **Perceivable**

    - Provide text alternatives for non-text content
    - Provide captions and alternatives for multimedia
    - Create content that can be presented in different ways without losing meaning
    - Make it easier for users to see and hear content

2. **Operable**

    - Make all functionality available via keyboard
    - Give users enough time to read and use content
    - Do not design content that causes seizures or physical reactions
    - Help users navigate and find content

3. **Understandable**

    - Make text content readable and understandable
    - Make web pages appear and operate in predictable ways
    - Help users avoid and correct mistakes

4. **Robust**
    - Maximize compatibility with assistive technologies
    - Ensure content remains accessible as technologies advance
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/accessibility/STD-APP-ACC-001-accessibility.md#22-legal-and-regulatory-requirements]

### 2.2 Legal and Regulatory Requirements

All applications must comply with:

- **Section 508** (United States federal agencies)
- **Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)** compliance
- **European Accessibility Act** (for EU markets)
- **State and local accessibility laws** as applicable

### 4.1 Getting Started

1. **Install Accessibility Tools**: Set up ESLint plugins and browser extensions
2. **Conduct Accessibility Audit**: Review existing applications for compliance gaps
3. **Create Component Library**: Build accessible, reusable UI components
4. **Implement Testing Strategy**: Set up automated and manual testing procedures
5. **Train Development Team**: Provide accessibility training and resources
6. **Establish Review Process**: Include accessibility checks in code reviews

#### ESLint Configuration for Accessibility

```javascript
// .eslintrc.js
module.exports = {
    extends: ['plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended'],
    plugins: ['jsx-a11y'],
    rules: {
        // Accessibility rules
        'jsx-a11y/alt-text': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/aria-props': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/aria-proptypes': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/aria-role': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/aria-unsupported-elements': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/click-events-have-key-events': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/heading-has-content': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/no-interactive-element-to-noninteractive-role': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/no-noninteractive-element-interactions': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/role-has-required-aria-props': 'error',
        'jsx-a11y/role-supports-aria-props': 'error',
    },
};
```

[standards/application/accessibility/STD-APP-ACC-001-accessibility.md#accessibility-testing-checklist]

#### Accessibility Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Keyboard Navigation**

    - [ ] All interactive elements are focusable with Tab
    - [ ] Tab order is logical and intuitive
    - [ ] No keyboard traps (except modals)
    - [ ] Skip links work properly
    - [ ] Arrow keys work for menus and tabs

- [ ] **Screen Reader Testing**

    - [ ] Content reads in logical order
    - [ ] All images have appropriate alt text
    - [ ] Form labels are properly associated
    - [ ] Live regions announce dynamic content
    - [ ] Error messages are announced

- [ ] **Visual Testing**

    - [ ] Text contrast meets WCAG AA standards (4.5:1)
    - [ ] Focus indicators are clearly visible
    - [ ] Content is readable at 200% zoom
    - [ ] Information is not conveyed by color alone
    - [ ] Text can be resized up to 200% without horizontal scrolling

- [ ] **Interaction Testing**
    - [ ] All functionality available via keyboard
    - [ ] Touch targets are at least 44x44 pixels
    - [ ] Hover and focus states are consistent
    - [ ] Timeouts have warnings and extensions
    - [ ] Error recovery is possible
page_texts.45:
[standards/application/accessibility/STD-APP-ACC-001-accessibility.md#testing-with-assistive-technologies]

#### Testing with Assistive Technologies

1. **Screen Reader Testing**

    - NVDA (Windows) - Free screen reader
    - JAWS (Windows) - Professional screen reader
    - VoiceOver (macOS) - Built-in screen reader
    - TalkBack (Android) - Mobile screen reader

2. **Voice Control Testing**

    - Voice Control (macOS/iOS)
    - Dragon NaturallySpeaking (Windows)
    - Windows Speech Recognition

3. **Switch Navigation Testing**
    - Single-switch scanning
    - Two-switch navigation
    - Head tracking devices

## Glossary

- **ARIA**: Accessible Rich Internet Applications - specifications for making web content accessible
- **WCAG**: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines - international standards for web accessibility
- **Section 508**: U.S. federal law requiring accessibility in government technology
- **Assistive Technology**: Tools and devices that help people with disabilities access technology
- **Screen Reader**: Software that reads text and interface elements aloud
- **Focus Management**: Controlling which element receives keyboard focus
